ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha 83dce9a815b2 (2026-05-05T09:51:41Z) modified src/sessionservice/session_store.js and removed the TTL argument from all Redis SET calls for session keys. Sessions were previously stored with SETEX and a 3600-second TTL, but after this change they are stored with plain SET (ttl=0, no expiry). Because Redis is configured with maxmemory-policy=noeviction, it cannot evict any keys when memory fills up. The unbounded accumulation of non-expiring session keys exhausted the 512MB maxmemory limit within ~7 minutes of the deploy, after which Redis rejected all write commands with OOM errors, blocking cart updates, new logins, and payment job enqueueing.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately: Run 'redis-cli FLUSHDB' or selectively delete session keys ('redis-cli --scan --pattern sess_* | xargs redis-cli DEL') to free memory, then restart Redis to clear fragmentation. 2. Temporarily change maxmemory-policy to 'allkeys-lru' via 'redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru' to allow automatic eviction while the code fix is prepared. 3. Revert commit 83dce9a815b2 in src/sessionservice/session_store.js to restore SETEX with a 3600-second TTL for all session writes, then redeploy session-service. 4. After deploy, verify with 'redis-cli TTL <key>' that new session keys carry a non-zero TTL and monitor used_memory to confirm it stabilizes below the maxmemory limit.
